headline: Waller: we can wait one meeting, September hike odds 63% to 50%, jobs report 8:30
stance: One Waller line took the September hike from 63% priced to 50%. Today's jobs report at 8:30 decides which half is right.

news.head: Waller: we can wait one meeting
news.body: At a Thursday event the Fed governor said to give disinflation a chance. He backed holding rates steady this month.

news.head: ISM services 55.4, prices paid 72.6
news.body: August services expanded faster than forecast, up 1.3pt from July. The 12-month prices-paid average hit 68.5%, highest since April 2023.

news.head: Yen clawing back part of Thursday's rally
news.body: USD/JPY 156.40 overnight (~4am ET). Nomura calls a 25bp BoJ move this month reasonable, three straight hikes its extreme case.

news.head: Payrolls consensus +58k after July's -23k
news.body: Unemployment seen holding at 4.1%, average hourly earnings at 3.0% y/y. TD Securities is at +95k and flags hawkish risk to its own forecast.

implications: Equities priced the hold in full Thursday. The long end priced almost none of it. One of the two is wrong and 8:30 picks.
A coin-flip meeting makes today's jobs report the whole decision. Only next week's CPI is left before the FOMC.

watch.head: Jobs report, 8:30
watch.body: The August print, first since July's negative headline. Above 40k reads hawkish into a meeting priced at even odds.

watch.head: Average hourly earnings, 8:30
watch.body: Seen at 3.0% y/y, down from 3.2%. Waller's case rests on disinflation, and wages are what he has to defend.

watch.head: Whether the long end joins
watch.body: The front end did Thursday's work alone. A soft print that finally moves the 30y is a different trade.

watch.head: Gold back at a three-year extreme
watch.body: Thursday's move put it in the 88th percentile of three years, new in the last three sessions. Spec net length is already at the 99th.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Four days of rate-vol build unwound in one session on Waller. The front end did all of it, the long end none.
He would consider hiking only if inflation accelerates first. CPI lands Sep 11, five days before the meeting.
Services prices paid at 72.6 is the counterargument, its 12-month average the highest since April 2023.
sections.positioning: Spec net length in 5-year Treasuries sits at the 100th percentile of three years, up seven points on the week. An extended long into a meeting now priced as a coin flip.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Best session since Aug 4, and it came from a Fed governor, not from earnings or data.
Nasdaq led, which is what a rate-hold trade looks like before it becomes a growth trade.
Breadth still lags. Fewer than half of Nasdaq names sit above their 50-day line.
sections.positioning: Spec positioning in VIX futures sits at the 9th percentile of three years, third straight week. An extended short in vol into an 8:30 release that settles the meeting.

single_name.note: Jefferies joined the insider-buy list Thursday. One insider rule fired, it trades above its 200-day, 2.8 days to cover.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Credit sat out Thursday. Investment-grade and high-yield spreads are still marked to Wednesday, so the rally has no confirmation there.
Equity-credit correlation sits at 0.66. A one-day equity move on a Fed comment does not drag credit with it.
Reserves fell below $2.90tn last week as the Treasury account built. The plumbing is fine, the cushion keeps thinning.
sections.positioning: Dealer investment-grade inventory sits mid-range, the 56th percentile of three years. Dealers are neither defending spreads nor stepping away from them.

ideas.line: 4 open · 0 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
